# Alice

> Alice is a free, open-source email client for macOS, Windows and Linux. It has a calm desktop inbox, a terminal app and scriptable command line, and optional AI that uses your own API key. Mail is stored on your device; there is no Alice server.

- Website: https://getalice.email
- Source code: https://github.com/get-alice/alice
- License: GNU AGPL v3
- Platforms: macOS, Windows, Linux (Android and iOS planned)

## What it does

- Connects Gmail and Outlook through browser sign-in, and any provider that offers IMAP and SMTP (iCloud, Fastmail, self-hosted).
- Shows every account in one inbox, with keyboard shortcuts for every action.
- One local service owns the mail store, so the desktop app, terminal app and command line always show the same mail and drafts.
- Ask Alice: optional summaries, answers and draft replies with OpenAI, Anthropic or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including local models. Only the message you ask about (or the newest 20 inbox messages for inbox questions) is sent, directly to the provider you choose.
- Answers calendar invitations (accept, maybe, decline) by email, and can add events to a calendar app or a connected Google, Outlook or CalDAV calendar.
- Suggests recipients from your own mail and from read-only address books (Google, Outlook, CardDAV, Mac Contacts).
- Blocks remote images until you allow them, so senders cannot track when you open a message.
- Stores passwords and sign-in tokens in the system keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service).
- Interface languages: English (US) and German.
